title: Kit calibration v1 — one kit's supplies and the evidence behind them
description: Validates a curriculum's kit_calibration.v1.yaml. This is the half of the old calibration contract that was never engine-wide: which supplies one physical kit offers, which of them has been photographed or listed, and the rules a lab must obey when it cites one. It is the only schema permitted to name its kit, because it is the kit's own contract — FR-P3-NO-LITERALS excludes it for exactly that reason and forbids every other schema from doing the same.

kit.description: Which kit this is, and how well it has been verified. reference_verification is what an official listing or photograph establishes; local_inspection is what someone has confirmed by holding the thing.

power.description: The kit may offer several supplies; that is a set, not a conflict. What is forbidden is a lab that does not declare which one it uses.

rails.description: Selectable rail positions. 'OFF' must be one of them.

enforced_by.description: For each kit premise, the exact schema constraint that implements it. A premise with no entry here is unenforced.

additionalProperties.description: A path of the form '<file> → <json pointer or dotted path>'.

kit_terms.description: Every fact in this file that is this kit's rather than any kit's, with the anchored pattern that matches it in prose. FR-P3-SPLIT reads this list to prove no kit fact survived in the engine-wide calibration, and FR-P3-NO-LITERALS reads it to prove no contract names the kit. Both match the pattern, never the bare value.

power_input.description: One supply the kit offers. A lab may cite an input only when its verification is verified_official — an unverified input must be sourced and photographed first, or a lab can cite a supply nobody ever saw.

evidence.description: The photograph or listing that establishes this supply exists. Null only while verification is unverified.

then.description: Verified means something was seen. A verified input with no evidence is the claim this schema exists to refuse.
